headline: Under AGI by 2031, factory operators use the later 2034 robot date to train and protect a wage they may still need.

whatTheyDo.text: 184 of 202 plan retraining: one press worker plans a forklift licence this year and maybe basic electrics if the union pays.
149 plan other job options: one worker would apply to nearby robot-using plants in the first year after AGI arrives.
132 save more: one operator puts 50 a month into a separate savings account.
32 organize with others: a worker presses the union for six months' notice and paid courses.
25 adjust family plans: one young worker postpones trying for a baby for a few years.

whatTheySay: **A longer warning is usable time:** people describe starting maintenance, electrical or inspection routes before robots reach the floor.
**A course needs a wage at the end:** midlife workers ask for paid training and posted jobs at viable pay.
**Retirement is conditional:** older workers ask for written income and household costs before deciding whether to stop shifts.
whatTheyThink: **Delay could squander the warning:** some privately admit they may wait until robots are installed before changing.
**A certificate alone cannot protect pay:** private thoughts return to real vacancies, safe practice and household costs.
**Later is not never:** older workers may still need wages at 66 if verified retirement income falls short.
howTheyFeel: **Anxiety dominates:** 157 of 202 are anxious as they picture needing work after 2034.
**Some feel room to move:** 31 are uneasy and none calm; several see years to build practical skills.
**A small group is alarmed:** 14 fear losing the hands-on job despite the later deadline.

differences.text: On the 1–5 worry scale, thin-cushion profiles average 3.069 (n=72), versus 2.714 for strong cushions (n=63).
Resistant profiles average 3.118 (n=68), versus 2.687 for adaptive profiles (n=67), on the 1–5 worry scale.
Late-stage profiles average 3.000 (n=40), midlife 2.938 (n=81) and early-stage 2.852 (n=81) on the 1–5 worry scale.

quotes.name: Yusuf Rahman
quotes.text: There are three other plants within half an hour of me, and one of them is putting in robot cells now. I wouldn't wait around to be asked.

quotes.name: Colin Schmidt
quotes.text: I'd rather earn a bit less and know I'm on next month.

quotes.name: Carlos Evans
quotes.text: A booklet without guarded line time would not make me an inspector.

least.name: Time to pivot
least.story: Of the 31 least worried, 26 are early-stage and 21 adaptive; their accounts describe training or earning before floor robots arrive.

most.name: Thin starting margin
most.story: All 14 most worried are early-stage, 11 resistant and eight thin-cushion; they fear the later deadline will still end their present work.

thoughts.text: I could waste the warning by putting off a change.
Robots still threaten my hands-on job, only later.
The longer warning gives me time to prepare another work route.
A new credential or present experience alone will not secure a viable job.
I may still need wages unless retirement income covers the bills.
I must protect household income while factory work changes.
